lyrics:
[Intro: one low piano note, distant choir pad, heartbeat kick]

[Verse 1: low male voice, intimate]
"I'm good." "Just tired." "Busy week."
You've got a hundred ways to never speak
You smile on cue, you laugh on time
You've got everyone believing that you're fine

[Pre-Chorus: female voice joins]
And you're so worn out from holding the door
Against everything you can't say anymore

[Chorus: huge drums, strings, both voices]
So be honest to God
If you can't tell anybody else
Honest to God
He's not shocked, he's not somewhere else
Say the ugly part, say the part that scares you
Say the thing you'd never say in prayer, too
He can take it. He's not fragile.
Be honest to God

[Verse 2: female voice, close]
There's a man in the gospels crying at a grave
There's a man in a garden begging for another way
There's a man on a cross saying, "Why have you gone?"
If Jesus prayed like that, then you can go on

[Pre-Chorus: male voice joins]
He's not asking for the version that you post
He wants the one at three a.m. the most

[Chorus: huge drums, strings, both voices]
So be honest to God
If you can't tell anybody else
Honest to God
He's not shocked, he's not somewhere else
Say the ugly part, say the part that scares you
Say the thing you'd never say in prayer, too
He can take it. He's not fragile.
Be honest to God

[Bridge: piano only, whisper growing to a roar]
I'm not okay. (Say it.)
I'm angry. (Say it.)
I'm scared. (Say it.)
I'm here. (I know. Stay.)

[Final Chorus: everything, then suddenly quiet]
So be honest to God
If you can't tell anybody else
Honest to God
He's not shocked, he's not somewhere else
Say the ugly part, say the part that scares you
Say the thing you'd never say in prayer, too
And he's honest back: you're loved.
Honest to God

[Outro: piano, one long breath out]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 80 BPM, 4/4, C minor, ending on a major chord. Dark, slow and cinematic, with a chorus that hits like a wave.

VOICE: A man with a low, close, gentle voice sings verse 1; a woman with a clear, steady voice sings verse 2. They join for the choruses at full strength. In the bridge one confesses in a whisper and the other answers softly in parentheses.

INSTRUMENTS: A low piano, a deep heartbeat kick, cinematic toms and a huge snare in the choruses, a string section, a dark synth bass, a wordless choir pad, a bright piano figure that arrives with the final line.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, piano note and heartbeat. 0:12 Verse 1, him. 0:38 Pre-chorus. 0:48 Chorus 1. 1:18 Verse 2, her. 1:44 Pre-chorus. 1:54 Chorus 2. 2:24 Bridge, piano and whispers. 2:46 Final chorus, cutting to quiet on the last two lines. 3:18 Outro, a breath out at 3:26.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Modern cinematic pop: dark, wide and dramatic, drums enormous, voices dry and close in the verses.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: 'He can take it. He's not fragile.' at 1:08.

THE REVEAL: The title sounds like the everyday exclamation, and verse 1 is one friend talking to another. Verse 2 at 1:18 shows Jesus weeping at Lazarus's grave, in Gethsemane and on the cross, and names him.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Hiding, exhausted, permitted, loved.
